solution.body:
$n\in [100,700]$

$n(A)=$ Total $-$ (multiple of $3$ + multiple of 4) + (multiple of 12)

Total $=601$

Multiple of $3=102,105,\ldots ,699$

$\begin{array}{l} n=699=102+(n-1)3 \\ \Rightarrow n=200 \end{array}$

Multiple of $4=100,104\ldots .,700$

$\begin{array}{l} n=696=108+(n-1)12 \\ n=50 \\ \therefore n(A)=601-(200+151)+50 \\ =300 \end{array}$

text: If $f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x^{3}\sin \left (\frac{1}{x}\right ), & x\neq 0 \\ 0 & ,x=0 \end{array} \right.$, then
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given the function:

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x^{3}\sin \left (\frac{1}{x}\right ), & x\neq 0 \\ 0, & x=0 \end{array} \right.$

we need to find its second derivative at specific points.

First, let’s compute the first derivative $f^{'}(x)$:

$f^{'}(x)=3x^{2}\sin \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )-x\cos \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )$

Next, the second derivative $f^{''}(x)$ is:

$f^{''}(x)=6x\sin \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )-3\cos \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )-\cos \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )-\frac{1}{x}\sin \left (\frac{1}{x}\right )$

Therefore, evaluating the second derivative at $x=\frac{2}{π}$:

$f^{''}\left (\frac{2}{π}\right )=6\left (\frac{2}{π}\right )\sin \left (\frac{π}{2}\right )-3\cos \left (\frac{π}{2}\right )-\cos \left (\frac{π}{2}\right )-\frac{π}{2}\sin \left (\frac{π}{2}\right )$

Since $\sin (\frac{π}{2})=1$ and $\cos (\frac{π}{2})=0$, this simplifies to:

$f^{''}\left (\frac{2}{π}\right )=\frac{12}{π}-\frac{π}{2}=\frac{24-π^{2}}{2π}$

Finally, note that $f^{''}(0)$ is not defined, as it involves terms like $\frac{1}{x}$ when $x=0$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: The shortest distance between the lines $\frac{x-3}{2}=\frac{y+15}{-7}=\frac{z-9}{5}$ and $\frac{x+1}{2}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z-9}{-3}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given two lines are represented as:

$\frac{x-3}{2}=\frac{y+15}{-7}=\frac{z-9}{5}$

and

$\frac{x+1}{2}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z-9}{-3}$

The formula for the shortest distance between two lines is:

$d=\frac{|\left (⃗{a}_{2}-⃗{a}_{1}\right )\cdot \left (⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}\right )|}{|⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}|}$

From the given lines:

$⃗{a}_{1}=(3,-15,9)$

$⃗{a}_{2}=(-1,1,9)$

$⃗{b}_{1}=(2,-7,5)$

$⃗{b}_{2}=(2,1,-3)$

Calculate the difference:

$⃗{a}_{2}-⃗{a}_{1}=(-1-3,1+15,9-9)=(-4,16,0)$

Next, compute the cross product:

$⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -7 & 5 \\ 2 & 1 & -3 \end{array}\right |=(16\hat{i}+16\hat{j}+16\hat{k})$

The magnitude of the cross product is:

$|⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}|=|(16\hat{i}+16\hat{j}+16\hat{k})|=16\sqrt{3}$

Calculate the dot product:

$(⃗{a}_{2}-⃗{a}_{1})\cdot (⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2})=(-4\hat{i}+16\hat{j}+0\hat{k})\cdot (16\hat{i}+16\hat{j}+16\hat{k})=-64+256+0=192$

Finally, find the shortest distance:

$d=\frac{|192|}{16\sqrt{3}}=\frac{192}{16\sqrt{3}}=4\sqrt{3}$

Thus, the shortest distance is:

$4\sqrt{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: For $α,β\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ and a natural number $n$, let $A_{r}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} r & 1 & \frac{n^{2}}{2}+α \\ 2r & 2 & n^{2}-β \\ 3r-2 & 3 & \frac{n(3n-1)}{2} \end{array}\right |$. Then $2A_{10}-A_{8}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We are given a determinant $A_{r}$ defined as:

$A_{r}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} r & 1 & \frac{n^{2}}{2}+α \\ 2r & 2 & n^{2}-β \\ 3r-2 & 3 & \frac{n(3n-1)}{2} \end{array}\right |$

We need to find the value of $2A_{10}-A_{8}$.

Let's calculate the determinant $A_{r}$. We can use properties of determinants or expand it directly. A helpful trick is to use row operations to simplify the determinant before expanding. Let's perform the following row operations:

Replace Row 2 with (Row 2) - 2 $\times$ (Row 1)

Replace Row 3 with (Row 3) - 3 $\times$ (Row 1)

The determinant becomes:

$A_{r}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} r & 1 & \frac{n^{2}}{2}+α \\ 2r-2r & 2-2(1) & (n^{2}-β)-2(\frac{n^{2}}{2}+α) \\ (3r-2)-3r & 3-3(1) & \frac{n(3n-1)}{2}-3(\frac{n^{2}}{2}+α) \end{array}\right |$

Let's simplify the entries in the new rows:

Row 2:

First element: $2r-2r=0$

Second element: $2-2=0$

Third element: $(n^{2}-β)-2(\frac{n^{2}}{2}+α)=n^{2}-β-n^{2}-2α=-2α-β$

Row 3:

First element: $(3r-2)-3r=-2$

Second element: $3-3=0$

Third element: $\frac{n(3n-1)}{2}-3(\frac{n^{2}}{2}+α)=\frac{3n^{2}-n}{2}-\frac{3n^{2}}{2}-3α=\frac{3n^{2}-n-3n^{2}}{2}-3α=-\frac{n}{2}-3α$

So the determinant simplifies to:

$A_{r}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} r & 1 & \frac{n^{2}}{2}+α \\ 0 & 0 & -2α-β \\ -2 & 0 & -\frac{n}{2}-3α \end{array}\right |$

Now, we can easily calculate this determinant by expanding along the second column, since it has two zeros. The expansion along the second column is:

$A_{r}=-1\cdot \left |\begin{array}{ll} 0 & -2α-β \\ -2 & -\frac{n}{2}-3α \end{array}\right |$

$A_{r}=-1\cdot \left ((0)\times (-\frac{n}{2}-3α)-(-2)\times (-2α-β)\right )$

$A_{r}=-1\cdot (0-(4α+2β))$

$A_{r}=-1\cdot (-4α-2β)$

$A_{r}=4α+2β$

Notice that the value of the determinant $A_{r}$ does not depend on $r$ at all! It's a constant value determined by $α$ and $β$.

Now we need to find the value of $2A_{10}-A_{8}$.

Since $A_{r}=4α+2β$ for any value of $r$, we have:

$A_{10}=4α+2β$

$A_{8}=4α+2β$

So, $2A_{10}-A_{8}=2(4α+2β)-(4α+2β)$

$2A_{10}-A_{8}=8α+4β-4α-2β$

$2A_{10}-A_{8}=(8α-4α)+(4β-2β)$

$2A_{10}-A_{8}=4α+2β$

The value of the expression $2A_{10}-A_{8}$ is $4α+2β$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: The mean and standard deviation of 20 observations are found to be 10 and 2 , respectively. On rechecking, it was found that an observation by mistake was taken 8 instead of 12. The correct standard deviation is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the correct standard deviation, we first need to adjust the mean and sum of squares of the observations based on the correction of the erroneous entry. The original erroneous observation was 8, and the correct observation is 12. The mean and standard deviation of the 20 observations before correction were 10 and 2, respectively.

The sum of all 20 original observations ($S_{\text{original}}$) can be calculated from the mean formula:

$\text{Mean}=\frac{\text{Sum of all observations}}{\text{Number of observations}}$

$10=\frac{S_{\text{original}}}{20}$

$S_{\text{original}}=10\times 20=200$

The corrected sum of observations ($S_{\text{correct}}$) will replace the incorrect observation (8) with the correct one (12):

$S_{\text{correct}}=S_{\text{original}}-8+12=200-8+12=204$

The corrected mean ($μ_{\text{correct}}$) is:

$μ_{\text{correct}}=\frac{S_{\text{correct}}}{20}=\frac{204}{20}=10.2$

To find the corrected standard deviation, we need the sum of squares of the deviations from the mean for both the original and corrected data. The original sum of squares ($SS_{\text{original}}$) is calculated from the original standard deviation formula, where $σ=2$:

$σ^{2}=\frac{SS}{n}$

$4=\frac{SS_{\text{original}}}{20}$

$SS_{\text{original}}=4\times 20=80$

To calculate the corrected sum of squares ($SS_{\text{correct}}$), we need to adjust $SS_{\text{original}}$ by removing the square of the deviation of the incorrect observation and adding the square of the deviation of the correct observation:

$SS_{\text{correct}}=SS_{\text{original}}-(8-10)^{2}+(12-10.2)^{2}$

$SS_{\text{correct}}=80-(-2)^{2}+(1.8)^{2}$

$SS_{\text{correct}}=80-4+3.24=79.24$

Finally, the corrected standard deviation ($σ_{\text{correct}}$) is:

$σ_{\text{correct}}=\sqrt{\frac{SS_{\text{correct}}}{20}}$

$σ_{\text{correct}}=\sqrt{\frac{79.24}{20}}$

$σ_{\text{correct}}=\sqrt{3.962}$

The corrected standard deviation is closest to the value given in Option B, which is

$\sqrt{3.96}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\left (1+x^{2}\right )\frac{dy}{dx}+y=e^{\tan ^{-1}x}$, $y(1)=0$. Then $y(0)$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine $y(0)$, we start by solving the differential equation given:

$(1+x^{2})\frac{dy}{dx}+y=e^{\tan ^{-1}x}$

First, we rewrite it in the standard form for a linear differential equation:

$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{y}{1+x^{2}}=\frac{e^{\tan -1x}}{1+x^{2}}$

Next, we find the integrating factor (I.F.):

$\text{I.F.}=e^{\int \frac{1}{1+x2}dx}=e^{\tan ^{-1}x}$

Multiply through by the integrating factor:

$y\cdot e^{\tan ^{-1}x}=\int e^{\tan ^{-1}x}\cdot \frac{e^{\tan -1x}}{1+x^{2}}dx$

This simplifies to:

$y\cdot e^{\tan ^{-1}x}=\int \frac{e^{2\tan -1x}}{1+x^{2}}dx$

Make the substitution $\tan ^{-1}x=t$, then $\frac{1}{1+x^{2}}dx=dt$:

$\int e^{2t}dt=\frac{e^{2t}}{2}+\frac{C}{2}$

Rewrite in terms of $x$:

$y\cdot e^{\tan ^{-1}x}=\frac{e^{2\tan -1x}}{2}+\frac{C}{2}$

Use the initial condition $y(1)=0$:

$0=\frac{e^{2\cdot \tan -1 1}}{2}+\frac{C}{2}$

Since $\tan ^{-1}1=\frac{π}{4}$:

$0=\frac{e^{π/2}}{2}+\frac{C}{2}⟹C=-e^{π/2}$

Thus, the solution is:

$y\cdot e^{\tan ^{-1}x}=\frac{e^{2\tan -1x}-e^{π/2}}{2}$

Evaluating $y(0)$:

$y(0)=y\cdot 1=\frac{1-e^{π/2}}{2}$

Therefore,

$y(0)=\frac{1}{2}(1-e^{π/2})$

Hence, the correct answer is:

Option B

$\frac{1}{2}\left (1-e^{π/2}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text: The number of triangles whose vertices are at the vertices of a regular octagon but none of whose sides is a side of the octagon is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Any 3 of the 8 vertices form a triangle: ${}^{8}C_{3}=56$ triangles.

A triangle with two sides of the octagon has three consecutive vertices; there are 8 such triangles, one for each middle vertex.

A triangle with exactly one side of the octagon uses one side (8 ways) and a third vertex adjacent to neither end of that side: of the other 6 vertices, the 2 next to the side are excluded, leaving 4. This gives $8\times 4=32$ triangles.

No triangle has three sides of the octagon, so the triangles with no side of the octagon number $56-8-32=16$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: The function $f(x)=\frac{x^{2}+2x-15}{x^{2}-4x+9},x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The function $f(x)=\frac{x^{2}+2x-15}{x^{2}-4x+9},x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ can be simplified to $f(x)=\frac{(x-3)(x+5)}{x^{2}-4x+9}$.

For $x=3$ and $x=-5$, $f(x)$ equals 0. Therefore, $f(x)$ is not one-one as it yields the same output for different input values.

The range of $f(x)$ is $[-2,1.6]$, indicating that $f(x)$ does not cover all possible real values. Consequently, $f(x)$ is not onto.

Thus, the function is neither one-one nor onto.

text: The interval in which the function $f(x)=x^{x},x>0$, is strictly increasing is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First note that  

$f(x)=x^{x}=e^{x\ln x},x>0.$  

Differentiating gives  

$f^{'}(x)=x^{x}\left (\ln x+1\right ).$  

Since $x^{x}>0$, the sign of $f^{'}(x)$ is the sign of $\ln x+1$.  Hence  

$f^{'}(x)>0⟺\ln x>-1⟺x>\frac{1}{e}.$  

So $f$ is strictly increasing for all $x>1/e$.  Among the given choices that corresponds to  

Option D: $\left [\frac{1}{e},\infty \right )$.

text: Let a conic $C$ pass through the point $(4,-2)$ and $P(x,y),x\geq 3$, be any point on $C$. Let the slope of the line touching the conic $C$ only at a single point $P$ be half the slope of the line joining the points $P$ and $(3,-5)$. If the focal distance of the point $(7,1)$ on $C$ is $d$, then $12d$ equals $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As per given condition

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y+5}{2(x-3)} \\ \Rightarrow \ln (y+5)=\dfrac{1}{2}\ln (x-3)+c \\ \text{Passes through}(4,-2)\Rightarrow \ln 3=\dfrac{1}{2}\ln 1+c \\ \Rightarrow c=\ln 3 \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow$ Curve is $(y+5)^{2}=9(x-3)$

Focal distance of $(7,1)=\frac{9}{4}+4=\frac{25}{4}=d$

$12d=75$

text: If the second, third and fourth terms in the expansion of $(x+y)^{n}$ are 135, 30 and $\frac{10}{3}$, respectively, then $6\left (n^{3}+x^{2}+y\right )$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $(x+y)^{n}$, $T_{r+1}={}^{n}C_{r}x^{n-r}y^{r}$, so

$T_{2}=nx^{n-1}y=135,T_{3}=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}x^{n-2}y^{2}=30,T_{4}=\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6}x^{n-3}y^{3}=\frac{10}{3}.$

$\frac{T_{2}}{T_{3}}=\frac{2}{n-1}\cdot \frac{x}{y}=\frac{135}{30}=\frac{9}{2},\frac{T_{3}}{T_{4}}=\frac{3}{n-2}\cdot \frac{x}{y}=\frac{30}{10/3}=9$

Dividing, $\dfrac{2(n-2)}{3(n-1)}=\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow 4(n-2)=3(n-1)\Rightarrow n=5$.

Then $\dfrac{3}{3}\cdot \dfrac{x}{y}=9\Rightarrow x=9y$.

$T_{2}=5x^{4}y=135\Rightarrow x^{4}\cdot \dfrac{x}{9}=27\Rightarrow x^{5}=243\Rightarrow x=3,y=\dfrac{1}{3}$.

$6\left (n^{3}+x^{2}+y\right )=6\left (125+9+\frac{1}{3}\right )=804+2=806$

Hence, the answer is 806.

text: Let $αβγ=45;α,β,γ\in \mathrm{ℝ}$. If $x(α,1,2)+y(1,β,2)+z(2,3,γ)=(0,0,0)$ for some $x,y,z\in \mathrm{ℝ},xyz\neq 0$, then $6α+4β+γ$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that $αβγ=45$ and $α,β,γ\in \mathrm{ℝ}$, consider the equation $x(α,1,2)+y(1,β,2)+z(2,3,γ)=(0,0,0)$ for some $x,y,z\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ where $xyz\neq 0$. To find the value of $6α+4β+γ$, follow these steps:

Express the given equation in matrix form:

$\begin{array}{l} αx+y+2z=0 \\ x+βy+3z=0 \\ 2x+2y+γz=0 \end{array}$

Since $x,y,z\neq 0$, the determinant of the coefficients matrix must be zero:

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} α & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & β & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & γ \end{array}\right |=0$

Calculate the determinant of the matrix:

$αβγ-6α-4β-γ+10=0$

Given $αβγ=45$, substitute this value into the equation:

$45-6α-4β-γ+10=0$

Simplify the equation:

$45+10=6α+4β+γ$

Thus,

$6α+4β+γ=55$

So, the value of $6α+4β+γ$ is 55.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift

text:
Let the first term of a series be $T_{1}=6$ and its $r^{\text{th}}$ term $T_{r}=3T_{r-1}+6^{r},r=2,3$,
............ $n$. If the sum of the first $n$ terms of this series is $\frac{1}{5}\left (n^{2}-12n+39\right )(4\cdot 6^{n}-5\cdot 3^{n}+1)$, then $n$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} T_{r}=3T_{r-1}+6^{r} \\ \Rightarrow \text{solving homogenous part} \\ T_{r}=3T_{r-1} \\ \Rightarrow x=3\text{is the root} \end{array}$

$\therefore T_{r}=a.3^{r}$

Solving for particular part

$\begin{array}{l} T_{r}=b.6^{r} \\ b.6^{r}=3b6^{r-1}+6^{r} \\ \Rightarrow 6b=3b+6 \\ \Rightarrow 3b=6 \\ \Rightarrow b=2 \\ T_{r}=a^{n}+a^{p} \\ T_{r}=a3^{br}+2.6^{r}\text{.... (i)} \\ T_{r}=3T_{r-1}+6^{r} \end{array}$

Putting $r=2$

$T_{2}=18+36=54\text{.... (ii)}$

Using equation (i) and (ii)

$\begin{array}{l} 54=9a+72\Rightarrow -18=9a\Rightarrow a=-2 \\ \therefore T_{r}=2\cdot 6^{r}-2\cdot 3^{r}=2(6^{r}-3^{r}) \\ \sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}T_{r}=2\sum 6^{r}-2\sum 3^{r} \\ =2\cdot 6\dfrac{(6^{n}-1)}{5}-2\cdot 3\dfrac{(3^{n}-1)}{2} \\ =\dfrac{3}{5}(4\cdot 6^{n}-5\cdot 3^{n}+1) \\ \therefore n^{2}-12n+39=3 \\ n^{2}-12n+36=0 \\ (n-6)^{2}=0 \\ \therefore n=6 \end{array}$

text: For $n\in \mathrm{N}$, if $\cot ^{-1}3+\cot ^{-1}4+\cot ^{-1}5+\cot ^{-1}n=\frac{π}{4}$, then $n$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $n\in \mathrm{ℕ}$, if $\cot ^{-1}3+\cot ^{-1}4+\cot ^{-1}5+\cot ^{-1}n=\frac{π}{4}$, then $n$ is equal to .

Given the equation:

$\cot ^{-1}3+\cot ^{-1}4+\cot ^{-1}5+\cot ^{-1}(n)=\frac{π}{4}$

we can use the identity for the sum of inverse cotangents. Starting with the first two terms:

$\cot ^{-1}3+\cot ^{-1}4=\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{3\times 4-1}{3+4}\right )=\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{11}{7}\right )$

Now, adding the third term:

$\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{11}{7}\right )+\cot ^{-1}(5)$

we apply the identity again:

$\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{11}{7}\right )+\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{n\times 5-1}{5+n}\right )=\frac{π}{4}$

Rewriting this to isolate the sum of the terms, we proceed as follows:

$\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{\left (\frac{11}{7}\times \frac{5n-1}{5+n}-1\right )}{\left (\frac{11}{7}+\frac{5n-1}{5+n}\right )}\right )=\frac{π}{4}$

This simplifies to:

$\frac{11}{7}\left (\frac{5n-1}{5+n}\right )-1=\frac{11}{7}+\frac{5n-1}{5+n}$

Solving the equation:

$\frac{55n-11}{5+n}-1=\frac{11}{7}+\frac{5n-1}{5+n}$

Further simplification yields:

$55n-11-35-7n=55+11n+35n-7$

Bringing the terms together, we get:

$48n-46=48$

Therefore:

$2n=94$

So finally:

$n=47$

text: Let $r_{k}=\frac{\int _{0}^{1}\left (1-x^{7}\right )^{k}dx}{\int _{0}^{1}(1-x^{7})^{k+1}dx},k\in \mathrm{ℕ}$. Then the value of $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{10}\frac{1}{7(r_{k}-1)}$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$r_{k}=\frac{I_{a}}{I_{b}}\text{, where}I_{a}=\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (1-x^{7}\right )^{k}dx$


[IMG]


$\left. \begin{array}{l} =\left (1-x^{7}\right )^{k+1}\cdot x\right ]_{0}^{1}-\int\limits _{0}^{1}(k+1)\left (1-x^{7}\right )^{k}\left (-7x^{6}\right )\cdot xdx \\ =-7(k+1)\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (1-x^{7}\right )^{k}\left (-1+1-x^{7}\right ) \\ I_{b}=-7(k+1)[-I_{a}+I_{b}] \\ \Rightarrow r_{k}=\dfrac{I_{a}}{I_{b}}=\dfrac{7k+8}{7k+7}=1+\dfrac{1}{7(k+1)} \\ \dfrac{1}{7(r_{k}-1)}=(k+1) \\ \Rightarrow \sum\limits _{k=1}^{10}\dfrac{1}{7(r_{k}-1)}=\sum\limits _{k=1}^{10}(k+1)=\dfrac{11\cdot 12}{2}-1=65 \end{array}$

text: Let $⃗{a}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k},⃗{b}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$ and a vector $⃗{c}$ be such that $⃗{a}\times (⃗{b}+⃗{c})+⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}=\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+13\hat{k}$. If $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=13$, then $(24-⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{c})$ is equal to $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Expanding, $⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}+⃗{a}\times ⃗{c}+⃗{b}\times ⃗{c}=\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+13\hat{k}$, so $(⃗{a}+⃗{b})\times ⃗{c}=\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+13\hat{k}-⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}$.

$⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -3 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -5 \end{array}\right |=-\hat{i}+22\hat{j}+17\hat{k},$

so $(⃗{a}+⃗{b})\times ⃗{c}=2\hat{i}-14\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$.

With $⃗{a}+⃗{b}=5\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $⃗{c}=p\hat{i}+q\hat{j}+r\hat{k}$,

$(⃗{a}+⃗{b})\times ⃗{c}=(q+r)\hat{i}-(p+5r)\hat{j}+(5q-p)\hat{k}.$

Comparing components: $q+r=2$ and $p+5r=14$ (the third equation $5q-p=-4$ then holds automatically), so $q=2-r$ and $p=14-5r$.

$⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=2p-3q+4r=2(14-5r)-3(2-r)+4r=22-3r=13$, so $r=3$, $q=-1$, $p=-1$.

Then $⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{c}=3(-1)+4(-1)-5(3)=-22$, so $24-⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{c}=46$.

Hence, the answer is 46.

text: Let $L_{1},L_{2}$ be the lines passing through the point $P(0,1)$ and touching the parabola $9x^{2}+12x+18y-14=0$. Let $Q$ and $R$ be the points on the lines $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ such that the $△PQR$ is an isosceles triangle with base $QR$. If the slopes of the lines $QR$ are $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}$, then $16\left (m_{1}^{2}+m_{2}^{2}\right )$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} 9x^{2}+12x+18y-14=0 \\ \left (x+\dfrac{2}{3}\right )^{2}=-2(y-1)\ldots (1) \end{array}$

Equation of tangent to (1)

$\begin{array}{l} t\left (x+\dfrac{2}{3}\right )=-(y-1)+\dfrac{1}{2}t^{2}\text{passes through}(0,1) \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{2}{3}t=\dfrac{1}{2}t^{2}\Rightarrow t=0,\dfrac{4}{3}\Rightarrow m=0,m=-\dfrac{4}{3} \end{array}$


[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \left |\dfrac{m+\frac{4}{3}}{1-\frac{4}{3}m}\right |=|m|\Rightarrow \left |\dfrac{3m+4}{3-4m}\right |=|m| \\ \Rightarrow 3m+4=m(3-4m)\text{or}3m+4=-m(3-4m) \\ 3m+4=3m-4m^{2}\text{or}3m+4=-3m+4m^{2} \\ 4m^{2}+4=0\text{(not possible) or}4m^{2}-6m-4=0 \\ m_{1}+m_{2}=\dfrac{3}{2},m_{1}m_{2}=-1 \\ \Rightarrow m_{1}^{2}+m_{2}^{2}=\dfrac{17}{4} \\ 16\left (m_{1}^{2}+m_{2}^{2}\right )=68 \end{array}$
